First, recall that

$$
{lim}_{s\to 1}f(s)=[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 1}\sqrt{5-s} \\ {lim}_{s\to 1}\frac{{e}^{1-s}}{1-s} \\ {lim}_{s\to 1}\,(1+5s)^{1/(2s)}\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we find the limits one by one.

- For the first component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 1}\sqrt{5-s} & =\sqrt{5-1} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 1}\frac{{e}^{1-s}}{s}=\frac{1}{1}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the third component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 1}\,(1+5s)^{1-s} & =(1+5\cdot 1)^{1-1}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{s\to 1}f(s)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, the limit of $‖f(s)‖$ as $s$ approaches $1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 1}‖f(s)‖ & =‖{lim}_{s\to 1}f(s)‖ \\  & =‖[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
